audit.action: cite a better source for the same coding
audit.reasoning: The coding (fixed-dominant, initial: rule '10 100 1000 10000') rests on the only reference grammar of the language, a 2020 593-pp PhD grammar by a fieldworker with her own recordings, and the deciding sentence is verbatim at the cited page and section. The file was not held before; it is now on file, so the blank evidence grade can be raised to held-and-verified. Nothing better exists: Glottolog's remaining entries are a bibliographic handbook, a mis-attached Congo-language grammar, Nyigina/Warrwa notes and McKelson's lesson books, and Agnew's own literature survey cites no phonology article or instrumental study. The description is thin in detail (one sentence, no secondary stress, author flags no prosodic analysis) but that limits refinement (rhythm/secondary stress stay uncoded), not the primary-stress classification, which is also consistent with the Marrngu relatives. Wishlist items

sources.citation: Agnew, Brigitte Louise. 2020. The core of Mangarla grammar. PhD thesis, University of Melbourne. xviii+593 pp. hdl:11343/241927
sources.quote: 'Primary stress falls on the first syllable of a word.' Also: long vowels occur mostly 'in the first (stressed) syllable of a word'; 'In unstressed syllables, all three [vowels] can be centred to a neutral [ə]'; clitics 'are unable to bear major stress within the word'; verbalising suffixes 'never take primary word stress'. No secondary-stress or rhythm statement; author notes 'the absence of a detailed prosodic analysis'.
